title: Unbeaten 249-Run Stand Puts Sri Lanka Within 30 Runs of Pakistan in Rawalpindi
excerpt: Dhananjaya de Silva (167 not out) and captain Kusal Mendis (117 not out) batted through Day 3 of the first Test, taking Sri Lanka to 404 for 4 against Pakistan's 434 for 9 declared, with Pakistan taking only one wicket all day.
body:
• Sri Lanka closed Day 3 of the first Test in Rawalpindi on 404 for 4, trailing Pakistan's 434 for 9 declared by 30 runs with six wickets in hand.
  • Dhananjaya de Silva is unbeaten on 167 and captain Kusal Mendis on 117; their unbroken fifth-wicket partnership is worth 249 runs.
  • It was a day of landmarks: de Silva's 14th Test hundred, in his first Test after giving up the captaincy, and a hundred for Kusal Mendis in his first Test as captain.
  • Pakistan took only one wicket all day — Kamindu Mendis, for 58 — and put down chances that let de Silva escape on 38.

Sri Lanka owned Day 3 in Rawalpindi. Resuming on 131 for 3, the visitors lost only one wicket all day and closed on 404 for 4, 30 runs behind Pakistan's first-innings 434 for 9 declared, on the back of an unbroken 249-run partnership between Dhananjaya de Silva and Kusal Mendis.

How the day turned

The morning belonged to patience. De Silva and Kamindu Mendis rebuilt steadily, with de Silva surviving a straightforward chance at first slip, where Saud Shakeel put him down on 38 — the moment the day turned on, Cricbuzz reported. Kamindu reached his fifty before Mohammad Abbas, rewarded for persistent bowling, had him caught for 58. That was Pakistan's only success. Kusal Mendis, captaining Sri Lanka in a Test for the first time, started fidgetily, while de Silva rode further luck — a tough chance at short leg and a dropped return catch — before accelerating.

"It was a day of landmarks: de Silva's 14th Test hundred, in his first Test after giving up the captaincy, and a hundred for Kusal Mendis in his first Test as captain."

Two captains, two hundreds

De Silva flicked Arafat Minhas past mid-on to raise his 14th Test hundred, then passed 150 in the final session. Kusal brought up his hundred with an upper-cut over the wicketkeeper's head off Razaullah, a shot he repeated for six in the same bowler's next over. Their stand is, per the match records, the highest fifth-wicket partnership in Tests at Rawalpindi, passing the 240 put on by Mohammad Rizwan and Saud Shakeel against Bangladesh in 2024. Bad light ended play early, with only 12 overs possible in the last session.

What it means, and what's next

Sri Lanka resume on Day 4 needing 31 runs to move ahead, with de Silva six runs short of his career best and the new ball due. Pakistan's route back runs through an early strike with that ball; every run Sri Lanka add from here builds first-innings leverage in a match that has become a contest of who blinks first on a flattening pitch. Brief scores: Pakistan 434/9 declared; Sri Lanka 404/4 (de Silva 167*, Kusal Mendis 117*, Kamindu Mendis 58; Mohammad Abbas 2-64).
